facts.statement: The genus contains a single species, Pendraig milnerae, which was named in honor of Angela Milner.
facts.quote: It contains one species, Pendraig milnerae, named after Angela Milner.

facts.statement: Pendraig is estimated to have measured 1 meter in length when alive.
facts.quote: In life it would have measured 1 m in length.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 1952 at the Pant-y-ffynnon Quarry in Wales by Kenneth Alexander Kermack and Pamela Lamplugh Robinson.
facts.quote: The holotype of Pendraig were found in the Pant-y-ffynnon Quarry in Wales in 1952 by Kenneth Alexander Kermack and Pamela Lamplugh Robinson

facts.statement: The fossils were originally misidentified as a coelurosaur and later classified as a species of Syntarsus (now Megapnosaurus or Coelophysis).
facts.quote: The fossils were originally thought to belong to a "coelurosaur" (in the outdated sense of the word) and even subsequently classified as a species of "Syntarsus" (now Megapnosaurus or Coelophysis).

facts.statement: Angela Milner and Susannah Maidment recently rediscovered the fossils, which had been stored alongside crocodile bones likely belonging to Terrestrisuchus.
facts.quote: Recently Angela Milner and Susannah Maidment rediscovered the fossils stored with some crocodile bones (likely Terrestrisuchus).

facts.statement: The fossils were formally named as a new genus of theropod in 2021.
facts.quote: The fossils were named as representing a new genus of theropod in 2021.

facts.statement: The holotype (NHMUK PV R 37591) includes an articulated vertebral series and pelvic girdle with missing spines and distal ends, plus a disarticulated left femur from the same individual.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen consists of NHMUK PV R 37591, "An articulated vertebral series and pelvic girdle comprising the two posteriormost dorsal vertebrae missing most of the neural spines, the three anteriormost sacral vertebrae and a small fragment of the centrum of the fourth sacral, a complete left ilium, a largely complete left pubis missing the distal end, a left ischium missing most of the distal portion, a largely complete right pubis missing the distal end, and a right ischium missing most of the dorsal and distal portions" a left femur that is from the same individual was found disarticulated from the main block.

facts.statement: Spiekman et al. classify Pendraig as a coelophysoid theropod in a polytomy with Powellvenator, Lucianovenator, and the clade containing "Syntarsus" kayentakatae and Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: Spiekman et al. recover Pendraig as a coelophysoid theropod, in a polytomy with Powellvenator, Lucianovenator, and the clade comprising "Syntarsus" kayentakatae and Coelophysidae.

facts.statement: During the Late Triassic, Pendraig lived in southwestern Britain on islands formed from folded Carboniferous Limestone.
facts.quote: During the Late Triassic, the areas of southwestern Britain Pendraig was found and lived in consisted of a series of islands made from Carboniferous Limestone that had been folded and pushed upwards.

facts.statement: The environment where Pendraig lived consisted of dry forests similar to those found in the Cayman Islands.
facts.quote: The environment would have been dry forests described as similar to the Cayman Islands.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Pendraig's small size may be due to insular dwarfism, but this is debated because the known specimen is sub-adult.
facts.quote: Due to its island habitat, the small size of Pendraig may result from insular dwarfism, where animals on islands get smaller to conserve resources. However, due to the specimen being sub-adult, it may or may not be the case.

facts.statement: The species was named in honor of Angela Milner, and the specimen belonged to a creature measuring nearly one meter in length.
facts.quote: La especie fue nombrada en homenaje de Angela Milner. El espécimen se halló en la cantera de Pant-y-Ffynnon y pertenecía a una criatura que mediría cerca de un metro de longitud.

facts.statement: Pendraig lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 215 million years ago in the Norian stage, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Triásico, hace aproximadamente 215 millones de años, durante el Noriense, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: Spiekman et al. determined that Pendraig is classified as a coelophysoid theropod in a polytomy with Powellvenator, Lucianovenator, and the clade including "Syntarsus" kayentakatae and the family Coelophysidae.
facts.quote: Spiekman et al. determinaron que Pendraig se clasifica como un terópodo celofisoideo, en politomía con Powellvenator, Lucianovenator, y el clado que incluye a "Syntarsus" kayentakatae y la familia Coelophysidae.

facts.statement: Due to its island habitat, Pendraig's reduced size could be the result of insular dwarfism, though this is uncertain because the specimen is sub-adult.
facts.quote: Debido a su hábitat isleño, el tamaño reducido de Pendraig podría ser resultado del enanismo insular, en el cual los animales en las islas tienden a ser más pequeños para conservar los limitados recursos. Sin embargo, ya que el espécimen es de un ejemplar subadulto, podría o no ser el caso.

facts.statement: Pendraig lived during the Carnian stage of the Triassic, between 237 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Pendraig (meaning "chief dragon" in Middle Welsh) is a genus of coelophysoid theropod dinosaur from South Wales.
